paragraph: A news report of March 2026 says the Earth observation component of Angola's National Space Program is built around the [ANGEO-1 satellite](<https://www.wearetech.africa/en/fils-uk/news/tech/angola-launches-259-million-earth-observation-satellite-project>), with a focus on precision agriculture. [Digital Earth Africa and SASSCAL agreed to build the AgriWatch dashboard](<https://digitalearthafrica.org/en_za/growing-resilience-together-digital-earth-africa-and-sasscal-collaborate-on-agriwatch/>) for crop-cycle, rangeland and rainfall monitoring, and it covers Angola among six states. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found since October 2023 says a government satellite-based farming service is in use. Establishing would need a government crop, drought, locust or land-use service using satellite data in service.

[In August 2026 the state agronomic institute ISABU issued a tender for computers to make maps and process satellite images for agricultural research](<https://burundi-news.com/articles/en/burundis-isabu-seeks-high-performance-computers-for-mapping-and-satellite-imager.html>). [IGEBU, the national mapping institute, says its cartography serves to identify and manage agricultural zones](<https://www.igebu.bi/Services/cartographie/>), and that its map work uses remote sensing. [Enabel's PAIOSA programme began satellite monitoring of 4,500 hectares of smallholder farmland in November 2021](<https://eos.com/blog/enabel-helps-african-farmers-by-using-sattech/>). The tender dates from the last twelve months. No source found since October 2023 says a government satellite-based farming service is in use. Establishing would need a government crop, drought, locust or land-use service using satellite data in service.

[In October 2025 AKADEMIYA2063 launched the AAgWa platform of satellite-based crop statistics and yield forecasts for Benin](<https://akademiya2063.org/press_releases/DERPIn_learning_event_CN_OCT_Benin.pdf>), built with the national agricultural research institute INRAB and the farmer platform PNOPPA. [INRAB built a model on satellite vegetation-index series with CIRAD to map farming systems in northern and central Benin](<http://agritrop.cirad.fr/615836>), which reached 60% accuracy. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found since October 2023 says a government satellite-based farming service is in use. Establishing would need a government crop, drought, locust or land-use service using satellite data in service.

[ANAM, the national meteorological agency, describes its ten-day agro-meteorological bulletin as a current product](<https://meteoburkina.bf/produits/bulletin-agrometeologique-decadaire/>) that carries NDVI and NDVI anomalies alongside rainfall, temperature and humidity anomalies. In the last twelve months, the newest update listed in October 2026 covers 13 to 19 October. [The PPACI-BF coordinator said 4,197 people had subscribed to the index insurance by 2025](<https://faso7.com/2025/11/10/burkina-faso-lassurance-climatique-indicielle-le-nouveau-filet-de-securite-des-agriculteurs/>), and that project assesses seasons with ANAM rain-gauge data and satellite data. No source found counts farmers, extension workers or districts reached by the bulletin. Mature would need a count of farmers, extension workers or districts receiving satellite-based advice, alerts or insurance.

[In March 2026 University of Botswana researchers used CHIRPS satellite rainfall and CHIRTS satellite-derived temperature data to compute drought indices](<https://doi.org/10.3390/cli14040077>), and tested them against national crop-yield data. [They also used CHIRPS rainfall estimates to regionalise Botswana into drought zones](<https://doi.org/10.1007/s00704-026-06154-6>), and recommended building Nino 3.4 and SOI indices into national drought forecasting and early-warning systems. [Digital Earth Africa and SASSCAL agreed to build the AgriWatch dashboard](<https://digitalearthafrica.org/en_za/growing-resilience-together-digital-earth-africa-and-sasscal-collaborate-on-agriwatch/>), which covers Botswana among six states. The first study dates from the last twelve months. No source found since October 2023 says a government satellite-based farming service is in use. Establishing would need a government crop, drought, locust or land-use service using satellite data in service.

[SODEXAM says it signed a partnership convention with JooL International on 10 August 2026](<https://sodexam.com/climat-et-agriculture-la-sodexam-et-jool-international-misent-sur-lintelligence-artificielle/>) to use meteorological data, AI and satellite technologies against climate risk in agriculture. [AICCRA said in May 2026 that the agriculture ministry can now draw seasonally updated satellite maps and forecasts of rice area and yield](<https://aiccra.cgiar.org/news/space-soil-cote-divoire-harnesses-riice-secure-its-rice-future>) from the adapted RIICE tool. It says this is the first time the ministry has had such data. Both date from the last twelve months. No source found since October 2023 says a government satellite-based farming service is in use. Establishing would need a government crop, drought, locust or land-use service using satellite data in service.

[On 14 January 2026 the national climate observatory ONACC launched a platform for drought and flood early warning, built on weather observation, satellite imagery and field data](<https://africa24tv.com/cameroun-catastrophes-climatiques-une-plateforme-de-lonac-pour-anticiper-les-crises/>). It says the platform serves agriculture among other sectors. In the last twelve months this launch followed [a 2023 pilot, cited by ONACC, combining satellite analysis and drought indices](<https://www.onacc.cm/fr/data>) to map flood and drought risk to crops in seven Far North localities. No source found since October 2023 says a satellite-based farming service publishes on a schedule. Operating would need such a service to publish bulletins, maps or forecasts on a schedule.

[SPACEBEL says it signed contracts on 16 June 2026 with the DRC research ministry to supply and maintain the RDC-SAT Earth observation satellite](<https://www.spacebel.com/en/news/the_first_%E2%80%98made_in_belgium%E2%80%99_commercial_satellite_for_the_democratic_republic_of_the_congo_a_landmark_contract_for_spacebel_000260/14>), which supports the National Centre for Remote Sensing. [In March 2026 that centre held the first coordination committee of a JICA project](<https://kt.cd/2026/03/30/projet-teledetection-le-cnt-et-la-jica-mettent-en-place-le-comite-conjoint-de-coordination/>) to equip it to supply satellite analysis to the agriculture ministry. [A World Bank-backed crop insurance pilot in Kasai-Central, held by the agriculture ministry, began paying compensation on 14 October 2026](<https://www.ecofinagency.com/news/2210-60021-dr-congo-compensates-17-180-farmers-under-climate-insurance-scheme>), first to 17,180 farmers. All three date from the last twelve months. No source found since October 2023 says a government satellite-based farming service is in use. Establishing would need a government crop, drought, locust or land-use service using satellite data in service.

[In September 2026 Kazakh deputy PM Zhaslan Madiyev said Congo and Kazakhstan are working to build and launch Congo's first Earth-observation satellite](<https://www.adiac-congo.com/content/technologies-spatiales-le-congo-se-prepare-lancer-son-premier-satellite-dobservation-171586>), meant to help monitor forest resources, agricultural and mining activity and flood-exposed zones. [FAO's GIEWS country brief, reference date 23 June 2026, reports from satellite-based imagery on rainfall in most croplands](<https://www.fao.org/giews/countrybrief/country/COG/pdf/COG.pdf>). Both date from the last twelve months. No source found since October 2023 says a government satellite-based farming service is in use. Establishing would need a government crop, drought, locust or land-use service using satellite data in service.

[As at August 2026 FAO GIEWS runs an Earth Observation portal for Comoros](<https://eo.apps.fao.org/country/index.jsp?code=COM&lang=en>). [It gives an Agricultural Stress Index and drought-intensity indicators from METOP-AVHRR satellite vegetation data](<https://eo.apps.fao.org/country/index.jsp?code=COM&lang=en>), which identify cropped land at risk of drought. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found since October 2023 says a government satellite-based farming service is in use, and none gives a publishing schedule or a count of farmers reached. Establishing would need a government crop, drought, locust or land-use service using satellite data in service.

No stage is set. [In March 2026 IGAD sought a consultant to monitor crop conditions across the IGAD region from satellite data](<https://web.archive.org/web/20260714184321/https://necjogha.net/igad-seeks-consultant-for-crop-monitoring-and-forecasting-to-strengthen-food-systems-resilience/>), a notice that covers the whole region. Nothing found since October 2023 names satellite data put to use in farming in Djibouti. No change has been found in the last twelve months. Preparing would need a ministry, agency or research institute in Djibouti to have used satellite or remote-sensing data in a farming study or pilot, or to be preparing a service that will.

[The CGIAR tool series says the WaPOR Digital Unit at the agriculture ministry uses a WaPOR-based tool](<https://cgspace.cgiar.org/server/api/core/bitstreams/ecbc9233-d7ab-4c68-ac2b-4ce6928ecb05/content>) It computes ten-day irrigation water use from 20 m satellite data. [In February 2025 the ministry's secretary general said Algerian Space Agency imagery helped control the locust invasion](<https://lesenjeuxeco.dz/lutte-antiacridienne-lasal-met-son-imagerie-satellitaire-au-service-de-la-clcpro/>). He said 23,000 hectares were treated preventively. In the last twelve months, the press reported in March 2026 that [the locust response relies on an early-warning system supported by ASAL satellite data](<https://www.independentarabia.com/node/644775/%D8%A8%D9%8A%D8%A6%D8%A9/%D8%A7%D9%84%D8%AC%D8%B2%D8%A7%D8%A6%D8%B1-%D8%AA%D8%AA%D8%AD%D8%B5%D9%86-%D8%B6%D8%AF-%D8%A7%D9%84%D8%AC%D8%B1%D8%A7%D8%AF-%D8%A3%D8%B1%D8%B6%D8%A7-%D9%88%D9%81%D8%B6%D8%A7%D8%A1>). No source found since October 2023 says a satellite-based farming service publishes on a schedule. Operating would need such a service to publish bulletins, maps or forecasts on a schedule.

[In November 2024 NARSS and the Ministry of Agriculture presented a remote-sensing crop map of the 2023-24 winter season](<https://www.dailynewsegypt.com/2024/11/05/narss-agriculture-ministry-launch-map-of-winter-crops/>). Each governorate inventoried wheat, clover and sugar beet. [In October 2025 NARSS and the agriculture ministry estimated nine strategic crop areas from satellite imagery and AI models](<https://www.elwatannews.com/news/details/8164622>). In the last twelve months, [FAO published on 24 June 2026 a 10 m Sentinel-2 crop type map of Mallawi, Minya for 2023-2024](<https://data.apps.fao.org/catalog/dataset/59eee02c-ff3f-43d1-a7d1-a85b087fb2bf>). It was made with two Egyptian ministries. No source found since October 2023 says a government satellite-based farming service publishes on a schedule. Operating would need such a service to publish bulletins, maps or forecasts on a schedule.

[A study dated December 2025, funded by the Ministry of Agriculture through the IFAD-supported IADP, mapped irrigated land in Dighe and Gala Nefhi](<https://repository.up.ac.za/items/24403df4-7cf1-4497-83cc-c278af581f1f/full>) from Sentinel-2 imagery for 2015-2024. [In September 2025 FAO's Desert Locust Information Service trained national locust information officers in Rome, Eritrea's among them](<https://www.fao.org/transboundary-plant-pests-diseases/news/detail/eritrea--tunisia-and-kenya-strengthen-locust-early-warning-capacities-through-fao-led-training/en>), on tools including Google Earth Engine. [FAO's GIEWS says remote sensing imagery showed that the June to September 2026 rainfall deficits significantly affected vegetation in Eritrean cropping areas](<https://reliefweb.int/report/eritrea/giews-country-brief-eritrea-30-september-2026>). The study and the GIEWS finding date from the last twelve months. No source found since October 2023 says a government satellite-based farming service is in use. Establishing would need a government crop, drought, locust or land-use service using satellite data in service.

[The Ethiopian Meteorology Institute's satellite bulletin for 21 to 30 September 2026 analysed vegetation greenness from METEOSAT products and TAMSAT rainfall estimates](<https://www.ethiomet.gov.et/products/dekadal-satellite-bulletin/satellite-bulletin-11-20-september-2026/>). [The institute issues the bulletin every dekad](<https://www.ethiomet.gov.et/products/dekadal-satellite-bulletin/satellite-bulletin-11-20-september-2026/>). In the last twelve months, [two national research institutes co-hosted training in Addis Ababa in June 2026 on satellite crop-mapping platforms](<https://english.aircas.ac.cn/newsroom/nu/202607/t20260706_1176333.html>). No count of farmers reached by the bulletin has been found. [An index insurance scheme run with WFP and Pula reached 122,000 smallholders in Amhara in 2023](<https://ethiopianmonitor.com/2024/05/03/new-crop-insurance-initiative-offers-farmers-lifeline/>), and that count belongs to the scheme. Mature would need a count of farmers, extension workers or districts receiving satellite-based advice, alerts or insurance.

No stage is set. Nothing has been found since October 2023 that says whether satellite data is used in farming in Gabon. No study, pilot or service by a ministry, agency or research institute that uses satellite or remote-sensing data in farming has been found. No change has been found in the last twelve months. Absent would need a source from the past three years that says no farming service or institution uses satellite or remote-sensing data.

[In March 2026 the project leads said the Ghana Space Science and Technology Institute and VITO are building GEOMAIZE maize yield estimation from Sentinel-2 time series](<https://geoglam.org/from-partnership-to-practice-advancing-yield-intelligence-and-food-security-through-geomaize/>). They say Ghana has a foundation for an operational pipeline. [In October 2026 the Ghana News Agency reported a germination index insurance pilot](<https://gna.org.gh/2026/10/gaip-promotes-germination-index-insurance-to-protect-farmers-against-climate-risks/>) in the Northern and Upper West regions. It merges station rainfall with satellite data. Both date from the last twelve months. No source found since October 2023 says a government satellite-based farming service is in use. Establishing would need a government crop, drought, locust or land-use service using satellite data in service.

No stage is set. Nothing has been found since October 2023 that says whether satellite data is used in farming in Guinea. No study, pilot or service by a ministry, agency or research institute that uses satellite or remote-sensing data in farming has been found. No change has been found in the last twelve months. Absent would need a source from the past three years that says no farming service or institution uses satellite or remote-sensing data.

[FAO's 2024 publication says the government's IFAD-supported ROOTS project developed a geospatial monitoring platform](<https://openknowledge.fao.org/items/f3175f42-56ff-4b85-892b-528dd124b73a>) covering rice production, vegetable gardening, mangroves, forestry, agroforestry and infrastructure. [In 2025 FAO said the Gambia GeoLab, a national Google Earth Engine platform built under ROOTS, turns satellite data into indicators](<https://www.fao.org/geospatial/news/news-detail/fao-presents-the-gambia-geolab-at-geo-for-good-summit-in-singapore/en>) on land cover, rice production and forests. [A GCA-funded Earth Engine platform of satellite agricultural indices was built, and 12 government departments were trained on it from April 2024](<https://www.weatherimpact.com/products/gambia/>). No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found since October 2023 says a government satellite-based farming service is in use. Establishing would need a government crop, drought, locust or land-use service using satellite data in service.

[In February 2026 FAO's GIEWS country brief for Guinea-Bissau said satellite-based data showed some dry spells affected crops in localized areas in 2025](<https://www.fao.org/giews/countrybrief/country/GNB/pdf/GNB.pdf>). [WFP Guinea-Bissau says it monitors rainy-season conditions every month](<https://docs.wfp.org/api/documents/WFP-0000168803/download/>) with CHIRPS rainfall and MODIS NDVI. [The meteorological institute says AGRHYMET trained the multidisciplinary crop-campaign working group in August 2026](<https://meteoguinebissau.gw/noticias/capacita%C3%A7%C3%A3o-dos-quadros-de-sistemas-de-informa%C3%A7%C3%A3o-da-guin%C3%A9-bissau-sobre-a-utiliza%C3%A7%C3%A3o-de-produtos-de-observa%C3%A7%C3%A3o-da-terra-pot/>) on satellite imagery, NDVI and yield simulation. The brief and the training date from the last twelve months. No source found since October 2023 says a government satellite-based farming service is in use. Establishing would need a government crop, drought, locust or land-use service using satellite data in service.

[NDMA says it publishes monthly drought early warning bulletins that draw on satellite imagery](<https://ndma.go.ke/drought-information/>). [Kenya's National Drought Management Authority operates the Drought Early Warning System](<https://ndma.go.ke/drought-information/>), which uses satellite imagery with ground stations to monitor rainfall, temperature and soil moisture. [In 2024 the ADM-Kenya project delivered four satellite drought and crop-condition products](<https://publications.admkenya.eu/Final_ADMKenya.pdf>), and the ministry plans to add them to its monthly bulletin. No count of farmers reached by the bulletins has been found. [The livestock insurance programme has covered 100,000 people in six years](<https://unfccc.int/sites/default/files/resource/Aligning%20KLIP%20to%20UNFCCC%20De-risking%20strategies%20to%20enhance%20adaptation%20finance.pdf>), and that count belongs to the programme. No change to the bulletins has been found in the last twelve months. Mature would need a count of farmers, extension workers or districts receiving satellite-based advice, alerts or insurance.

[In April 2026 Liberia's Environmental Protection Agency sought consultants to develop an Automated Decision Management System](<https://emansion.gov.lr/sites/default/files/documents/5a_REOI_INTERNATIONAL%20CONSULTANTS%20TO%20DEVELOP%20AND%20OPERATIONALIZE%20AN%20AUTOMATED%20DECISION%20MANAGEMENT%20SYSTEM.pdf>). It will integrate satellite imagery with meteorological and hydrological data. It will generate localised climate information for sectors including agriculture. The request dates from the last twelve months, and no source found says the system has been built. No source found since October 2023 says a government satellite-based farming service is in use. Establishing would need a government crop, drought, locust or land-use service using satellite data in service.

[FAO trained Libyan national stakeholders in Tunis on 20-23 April 2026 in remote-sensing workflows for land cover maps](<https://www.fao.org/agroinformatics/news/news-detail/tunisia-strengthens-geospatial-platforms-and-ai-tools-for-sustainable-water-and-oasis-management/en>), generated on the MERWAT geospatial platform. [In 2025 experts of the Grain Production Authority and Misrata's Agronomic Research Center trialled the GMES services MISBAR, GUETCROP and SAQIYA](<https://www.oss-online.org/en/GMES%26%20Libye>) on their own plots. [The Agricultural Research Center was trained in February 2024 on the MISBAR, MISLAND and GUETCROP tools](<https://projet.oss-online.org/GMES-Africa/en/blog/oss-hosting-representatives-libyan-agricultural-research-center-arc-training-workshop-seasonal>). The April 2026 training dates from the last twelve months. No source found since October 2023 says a government satellite-based farming service is in use. Establishing would need a government crop, drought, locust or land-use service using satellite data in service.

No stage is set. Nothing has been found since October 2023 that says whether satellite data is used in farming in Lesotho. No study, pilot or service by a ministry, agency or research institute that uses satellite or remote-sensing data in farming has been found. No change has been found in the last twelve months. Absent would need a source from the past three years that says no farming service or institution uses satellite or remote-sensing data.

[The Digital Hub for Agriculture, Forests and the Drought Observatory says it now operates a drought geoportal using CHIRPS, MODIS and SMAP satellite sources](<https://poledigital.ma/satellite-et-intelligence-artificielle-pour-le-developpementde-geoservices-agricoles-foncier-cultures-eau/>). It also runs crop maps from Sentinel-2 imagery and a farmer e-service with NDVI, SPI and SPEI maps. A FAO-funded agreement behind them closed on 30 May 2026, in the last twelve months. [In June 2024 Morocco's delegation told COPUOS that it is engaged in Earth observation projects with products in areas including agriculture](<https://www.unoosa.org/documents/pdf/copuos/2024/statements/9_Morocco.pdf>). [CGMS-Maroc, run since the early 2010s by the agronomic research institute with the meteorological service, uses satellite imagery to monitor cereal crops](<https://www.agrimaroc.ma/cgms-maroc-systeme-alerte-secheresse-prevision-rendements-cerealiers/>). No source found since October 2023 says a satellite-based farming service publishes on a schedule. Operating would need such a service to publish bulletins, maps or forecasts on a schedule.

[UNDP says its satellite-based geospatial assessment found up to 174,100 hectares of Madagascar cropland flooded by the February 2026 cyclones](<https://www.undp.org/africa/press-releases/cyclones-devastated-madagascars-poorest-communities-new-satellite-analysis-reveals>). UNDP is working with national and local authorities to prioritise recovery. [UNICEF Madagascar, with the EU Joint Research Centre and the water ministry, set up a drought monitoring system for the south using satellite rainfall and vegetation data](<https://www.unicef.org/madagascar/rapports/bulletin-dalerte-s%C3%A9cheresse-du-grand-sud-de-madagascar-2025>). The document notes that Madagascar has no national drought monitoring system. The UNDP assessment dates from the last twelve months. No source found since October 2023 says a government satellite-based farming service is in use. Establishing would need a government crop, drought, locust or land-use service using satellite data in service.

[In May 2026 AICCRA reported that it extended RIICE satellite rice monitoring to major irrigated and rainfed rice zones](<https://aiccra.cgiar.org/publications/institutionalization-riice-tool-agricultural-investment-planning-and-climate-risk>), with the Ministry of Agriculture, the Institut d'Economie Rurale and Mali-Meteo. It also prepared frameworks to operate the tool within national agricultural monitoring systems. [IWMI says the WaPOR-based Mali Drought Monitoring System was in beta in October 2025](<https://reliefweb.int/attachments/e772f400-92b7-402b-891d-d6210329e6f2/Drought%20monitoring%20-%20Mali-H053675.pdf>), and that the National Directorate of Agriculture is to run it once validated. The May 2026 report dates from the last twelve months. No source found since October 2023 says a government satellite-based farming service is in use. Establishing would need a government crop, drought, locust or land-use service using satellite data in service.

[In 2025 the Statistics from Space project tested an Earth-observation crop-type mapping workflow in Mozambique](<https://cgspace.cgiar.org/items/d99da2a4-6d50-4402-9a4a-83be3fe4260e>). It generated openly accessible crop type maps and statistics for Gaza, Manica and Zambezia for the 2024/25 season. [In June 2024 the project piloted satellite-based crop sampling at 92 sites in Gaza province](<https://www.cgiar.org/news-events/news/statistics-from-space-a-new-approach-to-agricultural-production-data-for-mozambique>). In the last twelve months, [in August 2026 FAO trained technicians of the National Irrigation Institute on a satellite dashboard of irrigation performance for the Lower Limpopo schemes](<https://www.fao.org/in-action/remote-sensing-for-water-productivity/news-and-events/news/news-detail/mozambique-strengthens-use-of-satellite-data-to-assess-irrigation-performance/en>). No source found since October 2023 says a government satellite-based farming service is in use. Establishing would need a government crop, drought, locust or land-use service using satellite data in service.

[The national meteorological office reads satellite data on vegetation in its ten-day rainy-season bulletin and gives advice to farmers and herders](<https://meteomauritanie.mr/documents/11/Bulletin_007.pdf>). [The office issues the bulletin every ten days; No. 007 is dated 31 August 2025](<https://meteomauritanie.mr/documents/11/Bulletin_007.pdf>). [The OSS says Mauritania has institutionalised two GMES services, both hosted on national servers](<http://www.oss-online.org/fr/GMESMauritania>). No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source counts farmers, extension workers or districts reached by the bulletin. [The TechghilAgro pilot's first season, in 2025, reached 102 rice farmers in Rosso and R'kiz](<https://sentinels.copernicus.eu/web/success-stories/-/empowering-agriculture-in-mauritania-with-sentinel-2-the-techghilagro-success-story>), and that count belongs to a pilot. Mature would need a count of farmers, extension workers or districts receiving satellite-based advice, alerts or insurance.

[UNCTAD says the Food and Agricultural Research and Extension Institute (FAREI) has been involved in CropWatch-ICP activities since 2021](<https://unctad.org/meeting/national-training-workshop-satellite-based-crop-monitoring-using-cropwatch-system>). FAREI held a CropWatch training workshop on 18-19 September 2025 to build staff capacity in satellite-based crop monitoring. [The Mauritius Cane Industry Authority and MSIRI say they have used GIS and remote sensing for sugarcane field management since the early 1990s](<https://edbmauritius.org/newsletter2024/september/drone.html>). [In October 2025 authors from the University of Mauritius and the government classified farmland in the Black River district from Satellogic images](<https://doi.org/10.1109/icares67579.2025.11371462>). No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found since October 2023 says a government satellite-based farming service is in use. Establishing would need a government crop, drought, locust or land-use service using satellite data in service.

[The CEOS Earth Observation Handbook says NASA Harvest, with FAO, adapted its satellite-based GEOCIF yield forecast model for the 2024 cropping season](<https://eohandbook.com/2026casestudies/malawi.html>) at the request of Malawi's Ministry of Agriculture. The National Committee on Crop Estimates recommended incorporating it into the crop estimates survey. [In August 2025 the Department of Climate Change and Meteorological Services piloted WFP's PRISM tool for drought monitoring in five southern districts](<https://www.maravipost.com/malawi-pilots-prism-drought-monitoring-tool-to-strengthen-climate-resilience/>). No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found since October 2023 says a government satellite-based farming service is in use. Establishing would need a government crop, drought, locust or land-use service using satellite data in service.

[In September 2025 Digital Earth Africa and SASSCAL agreed to build the AgriWatch dashboard](<https://digitalearthafrica.org/en_za/growing-resilience-together-digital-earth-africa-and-sasscal-collaborate-on-agriwatch/>), which covers Namibia among six states, for crop-cycle, rangeland and rainfall monitoring. [NASA Harvest says satellite tools and cropland masks from a USAID-funded FAO pilot were provided to the agriculture ministry and used in 2023](<https://www.nasaharvest.org/news/nasa-harvest-partners-fao-improve-agricultural-monitoring-across-malawi-namibia-and-kazakhstan>). In the last twelve months, [the agriculture minister said in November 2026 that the ministry had deployed the ERDAS APOLLO platform](<https://neweralive.na/namibia-calls-for-greater-use-of-geospatial-technology/>). It is a central satellite imagery repository to help monitor crop health and assess pastures. No source found since October 2023 says a government satellite-based farming service is in use. Establishing would need a government crop, drought, locust or land-use service using satellite data in service.
